text: In the race for the U.S. House seat in California's 17th district, Ro Khanna's documented record on Gaza and U.S. support for Israel marks a clear break from his Republican opponent. Khanna sponsored the Block the Bombs Act and a genocide-recognition resolution, declared Zero Aid to Israel at a 2026 Democratic National Committee meeting, introduced a June 2026 amendment striking Section 224 of the National Defense Authorization Act for its U.S.-Israel military integration, and in July 2026 co-sponsored a measure with Thomas Massie to block U.S. funding for Israel's military. He issued a ceasefire statement recorded by the Working Families Party in May 2024. In January 2026, he voted yea on an aid package carrying $3.3 billion for Israel, which he attributed to provisions Republicans inserted; he later voted no on the February consolidated bill. Tandon, by contrast, called Khanna's ceasefire advocacy naive in February 2024 and rejected the genocide label in October 2026 while emphasizing 1,200-plus Israeli victims. Khanna holds endorsements from CAIR Action, AROC Action, and Track AIPAC, while also drawing J Street PAC support.

editorial_correction.reason: The source contains several not-aligned votes, so one contrary vote is an incorrect exclusive claim. Preserve the January vote, its stated explanation and the later February No.
